SWC-107.name: Reentrancy
SWC-107.description: An external call to an untrusted contract is made before internal state variables (like balances) are updated. The external contract can recursively call back into the vulnerable contract and drain funds.
SWC-107.remediation: Apply the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern: update state variables before making external calls. Alternatively, inherit and use OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard modifier (nonReentrant).

SWC-115.name: Authorization through tx.origin
SWC-115.description: Using tx.origin for authentication or authorization checks allows phishing attacks where an intermediate malicious contract tricks an authorized user into calling it, passing authorization through.
SWC-115.remediation: Replace tx.origin with msg.sender for access control checks. tx.origin represents the original sender of the transaction, whereas msg.sender represents the immediate caller.

SWC-105.name: Unprotected Ether Withdrawal
SWC-105.description: Functions that transfer Ether or drain contract balances lack appropriate access control modifiers, allowing arbitrary external callers to withdraw contract funds.
SWC-105.remediation: Enforce strict access control modifiers such as onlyOwner or an authorized role manager, and verify caller permissions before executing asset transfers.

SWC-106.name: Unprotected SELFDESTRUCT
SWC-106.description: A selfdestruct instruction is callable by unauthorized users, allowing attackers to destroy the contract bytecode and force-send remaining Ether to an arbitrary address.
SWC-106.remediation: Avoid selfdestruct in modern Solidity contracts. If mandatory, restrict invocation strictly to a multisig governance address with a timelock.

SWC-104.name: Unchecked Call Return Value
SWC-104.description: The return value of a low-level call (e.g. address.send() or address.call()) is not verified. If the external call fails, execution continues silently, resulting in inconsistent state.
SWC-104.remediation: Always check the boolean success flag returned by low-level calls: (bool success, ) = recipient.call{value: amount}(''); require(success, 'Transfer failed');.

SWC-116.name: Block Values as a Proxy for Time (Timestamp Dependence)
SWC-116.description: Using block.timestamp or now for critical logic such as pseudo-random number generation or strict time locks allows miners/validators to manipulate block timestamps within ~15-second windows.
SWC-116.remediation: Never use block.timestamp for randomness (use Chainlink VRF). For time locks, allow a sufficient tolerance margin of several minutes.

SWC-100.name: Function Default Visibility
SWC-100.description: Functions that omit explicit visibility specifiers default to public in older Solidity versions, unintentionally exposing internal helper routines to external invocation.
SWC-100.remediation: Explicitly specify visibility (external, public, internal, private) for every function declaration.
